concentration_time_figure.caption_quote: Residual concentrations of lysostaphin (blue, circles) and Lst-HDD (orange, triangles) in rat plasma. The mean values over n = 4 rats are shown

bioanalytical_method: Sandwich ELISA: rabbit anti-lysostaphin antiserum capture (1/500), murine 2F9 monoclonal antibody detection (1/300), HRP-conjugated anti-mouse secondary, TMB substrate, absorbance at 450 nm; terminal half-life and AUC by non-compartmental analysis
bioanalytical_quote: The residual concentration of lysostaphin and Lst-HDD in rat plasma was measured using sandwich ELISA.
notes: IMPORTANT SPECIES CAVEAT: all pharmacokinetic work in this paper was done in RATS (female Wistar, n = 4 per group), not mice. The body does state mouse half-life values for lysostaphin, Cpl-1 and LytA, but only in the Introduction as citations of prior literature, not as data generated here: 'The estimated serum half-life of anti-staphylococcal lysin lysostaphin in mice was less than 1 h, and the half-life times of anti-pneumococcal lysins Cpl-1 and LytA were measured to be 20.5 and 22.5 min, respectively.' Cpl-1 and LytA were never produced, administered or assayed in this study and are therefore not listed as agents. Reported PK: lysostaphin terminal t1/2 1.5 ± 0.7 h and AUC 3.5 ± 2.4 mg·h/L; Lst-HDD terminal t1/2 3.1 ± 0.6 h and AUC 9.1 ± 2.8 mg·h/L. No Cmax or Tmax was determined; the first sample was at 25 min, where concentrations were 2.8 ± 0.2 µg/mL (lysostaphin) and 1.6 ± 0.1 µg/mL (Lst-HDD) against a theoretical post-injection concentration of ~50 µg/mL, indicating ~95% had already been eliminated. Amino-acid sequences appear only as a figure graphic (Fig. 1B) and are not extractable from the body text.
